stem:
Sonia writes $90 = 9 \times 10$ and wants the prime factorisation of $90$ by breaking composite factors until only primes remain.

Which plan is correct?

options.text: Report the words prime factor as the factorisation of $90$.
The product $2 \times 3 \times 3 \times 5$ produces the breaking of $9$ and $10$, so she starts from those primes and only then names $9$ and $10$.
Square $9$ and $10$ and treat $81 \times 100$ as the prime factorisation of $90$.

teacher.key_rationale: Break each composite until only primes remain: 9=3×3 and 10=2×5, so 90=2×3×3×5. Naming the label, starting from the finished prime product, or squaring the composites all miss that hinge.
